messages:
maya: Quick Q — we have a config-only change to the default model routing (alias swap). Is this a patch bump or a minor?

sam: Can you paste the PR diff or the key line?

maya: main change: `model_alias: "redwood/v1"` -> `model_alias: "redwood/v1-quant"`  (no API schema changes, only defaults)

chris: If there's no API contract change semver purists say patch, but it's a user-visible behavioral change so some teams do minor.

leo: My vote: patch if we make it reversible + document it clearly. If it's hard to opt out then minor.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary -> eng-staging at 2024-11-03T09:12Z. Rollback window: 30m. Trigger: PR #4821.

sam: Runbook proposal: monitor 5m error rate, p50/p95 latency, and cost/tokens delta. If error rate > 0.5% OR p95 latency +50ms => rollback with `deploy rollback --to-alias redwood/v1`.

maya: Runbook looks good. Dedicated/DC customers must opt-in; this change only flips the hosted default.

ana: PM note: include a clear line in release notes: "Default model routing changed to quantized variant (cost saving) — opt-out available". Call out perf + cost impact.

chris: Tagging suggestion: keep it as a patch (e.g., `v1.4.2` -> `v1.4.3`) and add a release note header `behavioral change: model routing default` and an explicit migration note.

sam: Also note: customers who pin explicit model versions (sha/pinned alias) are unaffected. Add that to the docs.

leo: If canary shows latency regression > 50ms or increased error rate we'll abort. Agreed on thresholds.

maya: Decision: patch bump + doc & runbook. I'll add `breaking_behavior: true` in the release-metadata so it's flagged in the Console.

sam: I'll cut `v1.4.3` after merge and trigger canary.

maya: Thanks — I'll draft release notes and add the opt-out snippet.

chris: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary complete: 15m, no errors, latency delta +12ms, cost -8% vs baseline. Marking for rollout to prod.

maya: Nice. Closing loop; will follow up with final release note link once published.
